title: feat(spec): ConnectorSourcePullRequest carries the caller package (callerPackageId), so a pull can read its mapping by (package, name)

_Requested by **Yibo Wang** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01BVUyyPie8gHwoPM18iABwB?thread=cmsg_01BVUyyPie8gHwoPM18iABwBWTahRMNCkb3Kmmwx8xcevN)_

Fixes #32078

Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: none — the new key is a service-contract request field that the runtime job binder fills; nothing a metadata author writes changes (`JobSchema.pull`, `MappingSchema` and `connectorSource` are untouched), so no `skills/**` or `content/docs/**` sentence teaches it
Prior rulings read: connectorsourcepullrequest,pullconnectorsource,appid,packageid → 9 hits; ADR-0019 D4, ADR-0029 D9.7, ADR-0045 Decision §7, ADR-0068 D3, ADR-0086 D3, ADR-0086 D4, ADR-0086 D5, ADR-0086 D7, ADR-0090 D9; thread: none; repo: objectstack-ai/objectstack. Every hit is on `packageId` as an item's OWNING package (permission sets, namespaces, materialization); none rules on how a caller names its package. The governing record is ADR-0150 D3 (not a term hit), which this card implements the spec half of.
Carried: #32071 (`domain:server#3`, its pull half): the runtime job binder passes the package that declares the job as `callerPackageId`, and `connector-pull.ts` reads the mapping by D3 from it. #31700 (`Blocked-by: #32078`) waits on that reader. Until #32071 lands, no implementation reads the key, and every pull reads by no package, as today.

Red-line review: the epic (#31527) asks for one before landing; the seat runs it.

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：`ConnectorSourcePullRequest`（`pullConnectorSource` 的请求）新增可选字段 `callerPackageId`（`string | null`），让作业的拉取能带上作业所在的包。
- 为什么改：ADR-0150 D3 要求按（包, 名称）读 mapping；之前请求里没有任何字段能把作业的包带到拉取端，#32071 的拉取半段无从实现。
- 风险与回滚：只放宽，类型层面纯新增；不带该字段等于"不按包读"，与今天完全一致；目前没有任何实现读取它。回滚即还原本 PR。
- 先看：`packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts` 里 `ConnectorSourcePullRequest` 新字段与 TSDoc；`automation-service.test.ts` 末尾新增的 describe。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec exec vitest run src/contracts/automation-service.test.ts`，预期 20 个测试全绿。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。

## What changes

- **`ConnectorSourcePullRequest.callerPackageId?: string | null`** (`packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts`). The package the caller belongs to, so `mapping` is read by `(package, name)` (ADR-0150 D3); for a job's pull it is the package that declares the job, with no inference that the name answers that package's own mapping (in a multi-package artifact the binder finds the mapping in any package body, so the read may go through the closure or be refused as outside it; contract review 6762357312, should-fix 1). The TSDoc states both arms: a package id resolves from that package (own item, else the unique holder in its declared closure plus `sys`; not found when nothing holds the name; a refusal naming every candidate when it is held twice in reach, only outside the closure, or only by an environment-authored item); **absent (omitted, `null` or `''`) is a read by no package, exactly as today** — the bare name, read as a caller with no package. It also says an implementation written before the key still satisfies the contract and reads by no package.
- **Spelling and type — the house precedent.** `packages/spec/src/contracts/` spells a caller's package for an ADR-0150 D3 read as `callerPackageId`, typed `string | null` (`OwnershipQueueCallerPackage`, `ownership-queue-service.ts`, on `resolveQueue` / `expandMembers` / `isMember`; the same spelling is the resolver's parameter, `registry.ts` `resolveItem(type, name, callerPackageId?)`). The bare `packageId` in the sibling contracts (`ownership-queue-service.ts` `ResolvedQueue.packageId`, `security-service.ts`, `realtime-service.ts`, `objectql-engine.ts` hook options, `automation-service.ts` connector rows) names an item's OWNING package or a filter, not the package a read is made from; `appId` appears only as an app-lifecycle argument. So the caller key is `callerPackageId`, with the same value type and the same absent meaning (omitted, `null` or `''`).
- **Pins** (`packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.test.ts`, new top-level `describe`, the shared harness file for this contract):
  - type level, compiled by `check:test-typecheck`: `callerPackageId` is exactly `OwnershipQueueCallerPackage | undefined`; the request's keys are exactly `mapping | context | environmentId | callerPackageId`; `{ mapping: string }` alone still satisfies the contract (lit control); a package object is refused (`@ts-expect-error`);
  - runtime: a request without the key and with it (`'com.acme.crm'`, `null`, `''`, beside `environmentId`) are all accepted by an implementation written before the key;
  - doc: the TSDoc above the field carries the absent-value sentence, `ADR-0150 D3`, "the package that declares the job" and the precedent's name.
- **Baselines:** `packages/spec/api-surface/contracts.json` and `export-origins/contracts.json` list `ConnectorSourcePullRequest (interface)` by symbol only; a new member moves neither (`check:api-surface` and `check:export-origins` green, below). The contract has no zod twin and no conformance baseline (`git grep ConnectorSourcePullRequest` at fe1249b7: the contract, its two baselines by name, service-automation's engine and three CHANGELOG lines).
- **Changeset:** `@objectstack/spec` patch, carrying the declaration lines (`Metadata-protocol: none` grades `patch`; the ownership-queue precedent `.changeset/31734-queue-caller-package.md` is the same shape).

Out of scope, untouched: the runtime binder passing the package and `connector-pull.ts` reading by D3 (#32071), `ExecutionContext`.

## Acceptance notes

- No implementation reads `callerPackageId` yet, and the TSDoc says so in contract terms ("an implementation written before it … reads by no package whatever the caller sends"), so the key advertises nothing the runtime does not deliver today.
- `packages/runtime` test-layer typecheck first read 1 problem on a fresh worktree: `organization-ownership-boot-guard.turso-remote.kernel.test.ts` TS2307 `Cannot find module '@objectstack/driver-turso'` — that package's `dist` was not in the `runtime^...` closure build. After `turbo run build --filter=@objectstack/driver-turso...` the same typecheck is green; not a defect of this change.
